links.note: The key is that pi is irrational, against the claims that it is exactly 22/7 or rational. That 22/7 is only an approximation because pi cannot be written as a fraction is this concept, not the definition of pi as a ratio (1432).
One round of a radius-35 m track is 2 x 22/7 x 35 = 220 m. Straight application of C = 2 pi r; the distractor 110 is pi r, omitting the 2.
One revolution covers the circumference 22/7 x 56 = 176 cm, so 100 revolutions give 176 m. The whole calculation is C from the diameter, plus a unit conversion.
Because C = 2 pi r is linear in r, circumferences in the ratio 5:4 force radii in the same 5:4. The trap 25:16 treats the relation as quadratic, as it would be for areas.
The stagger exists because each lane's CURVED portions are arcs of different radii, so their lengths differ. It is the arc length of a part-circle that determines it, rather than any area formula.
Edging a radius-7 m garden needs C = 44 m, costing 44 x 28 = Rs 1,232 against a Rs 1,500 budget. The only formula used is C = 2 pi r.
A radius-3.5 m bed has C = 22 m, so the border costs Rs 880 and Rs 500 falls short. Again the circumference is the whole of the mathematics.
176 cm per rotation into 100,000 cm gives 568.18, rounded UP to 569 complete rotations. The circumference is computed from the diameter and then divided into the distance.
